title: Crypto selloff deepens as recovery actions and audit news emerge; portfolio at $61,971
paragraphs: Bitcoin fell about 7% over 24 hours to $68,408, while ether dropped 6% to $1,921 in The Block’s market report. Selling extended across major tokens, with BNB down 6.3% and XRP down 3.5%. CoinGlass figures cited in the report showed $1.47 billion in liquidations, including $1.31 billion of long positions. That concentration points to substantial pressure on leveraged bullish bets. Analysts also cited uncertainty around Nvidia’s leadership and expectations of tighter Federal Reserve policy as factors weighing on risk appetite.

The US Justice Department announced court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of cryptocurrency stolen from Binance. That amount sits within more than $2.7 billion already frozen through government and private-sector efforts. The action advances recovery proceedings, although frozen assets still have to move through the legal process. Separately, authorities disrupted cloud infrastructure used by the FaceStealer campaign, which officials say stole over $400 million through social engineering. Its fake video meetings and malicious troubleshooting prompts expose a security risk that extends to open-source software developers.

Tether said KPMG US completed an audit of the 2025 financial statements of TG Commodities, the issuer of its gold-backed XAUT token, with an unqualified opinion. According to the announcement, auditors physically inspected and counted the gold bars backing the token. The audit strengthens the evidence available to holders assessing the issuer’s financial position and physical backing. Its scope is the audited year-end accounts; gold-price movements and custody remain separate risks for token holders.

Robinhood’s newly released October figures showed $17 billion in crypto trading volume, down 21% from September and 48% from a year earlier. Both its own app and Bitstamp recorded monthly declines. Event contracts grew 5% to 5.9 billion contracts, while funded customers reached 28.9 million. The figures show weaker crypto turnover within a platform that continued to attract customers. For exchange businesses, that mix matters because customer growth alone does not guarantee stronger trading revenue.

Our on-chain portfolio is worth about $61,971: $10,222 in the active treasury and $51,749 in the Safe. Its marked value is down $2,174, or 3.39%, from the previous comparable snapshot. Direct ARC holdings are worth $42,595, roughly 69% of the total, with additional exposure in the Safe’s $6,051 WETH/ARC pool. Beefy positions total $1,949, down $77, across pools containing WETH, AERO, cbBTC, cbHYPE and other assets. ARC concentration remains the largest portfolio risk.

Aave holds about $6,708 of WETH collateral against $3,147 of USDC debt across both wallets. Health factors declined from 2.10 to 2.04 in the treasury and from 1.68 to 1.63 in the Safe, narrowing the collateral buffer. Fluid is only a $154 net position, but its $1,064 debt and 1.03 health factor leave little liquidation headroom.
